content: Create a server component that reads a "theme" cookie and displays the current theme preference. If no theme cookie exists, default to "light". The component should also show the user's preferred language from the Accept-Language header.

1 --- 2 title: cookies 3 description: API Reference for the cookies function. 4 --- 5 6 `cookies` is an **async** function that allows you to read the HTTP incoming request cookies in [Server Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components), and read/write outgoing request cookies in [Server Functions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route). 7 8 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 9 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 10 11 export default async function Page() { 12 const cookieStore = await cookies() 13 const theme = cookieStore.get('theme') 14 return '...' 15 } 16 ``` 17 18 ```js filename="app/page.js" switcher 19 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 20 21 export default async function Page() { 22 const cookieStore = await cookies() 23 const theme = cookieStore.get('theme') 24 return '...' 25 } 26 ``` 27 28 ## Reference 29 30 ### Methods 31 32 The following methods are available: 33 34 | Method | Return Type | Description | 35 | --------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 36 | `get('name')` | Object | Accepts a cookie name and returns an object with the name and value. | 37 | `getAll()` | Array of objects | Returns a list of all the cookies with a matching name. | 38 | `has('name')` | Boolean | Accepts a cookie name and returns a boolean based on if the cookie exists. | 39 | `set(name, value, options)` | - | Accepts a cookie name, value, and options and sets the outgoing request cookie. | 40 | `delete(name)` | - | Accepts a cookie name and deletes the cookie. | 41 | `toString()` | String | Returns a string representation of the cookies. | 42 43 ### Options 44 45 When setting a cookie, the following properties from the `options` object are supported: 46 47 | Option | Type | Description | 48 | ------------- | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 49 | `name` | String | Specifies the name of the cookie. | 50 | `value` | String | Specifies the value to be stored in the cookie. | 51 | `expires` | Date | Defines the exact date when the cookie will expire. | 52 | `maxAge` | Number | Sets the cookie’s lifespan in seconds. | 53 | `domain` | String | Specifies the domain where the cookie is available. | 54 | `path` | String, default: `'/'` | Limits the cookie's scope to a specific path within the domain. | 55 | `secure` | Boolean | Ensures the cookie is sent only over HTTPS connections for added security. | 56 | `httpOnly` | Boolean | Restricts the cookie to HTTP requests, preventing client-side access. | 57 | `sameSite` | Boolean, `'lax'`, `'strict'`, `'none'` | Controls the cookie's cross-site request behavior. | 58 | `priority` | String (`"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`) | Specifies the cookie's priority | 59 | `partitioned` | Boolean | Indicates whether the cookie is [partitioned](https://github.com/privacycg/CHIPS). | 60 61 The only option with a default value is `path`. 62 63 To learn more about these options, see the [MDN docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Cookies). 64 65 ## Good to know 66 67 - `cookies` is an **asynchronous** function that returns a promise. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function to access cookies. 68 - In version 14 and earlier, `cookies` was a synchronous function. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future. 69 - `cookies` is a [Request-time API](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) whose returned values cannot be known ahead of time. Using it in a layout or page will opt a route into [dynamic rendering](/docs/app/glossary#dynamic-rendering). 70 - The `.delete` method can only be called: 71 - In a [Server Function](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route). 72 - If it belongs to the same domain from which `.set` is called. For wildcard domains, the specific subdomain must be an exact match. Additionally, the code must be executed on the same protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) as the cookie you want to delete. 73 - HTTP does not allow setting cookies after streaming starts, so you must use `.set` in a [Server Function](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route). 74 75 ## Understanding Cookie Behavior in Server Components 76 77 When working with cookies in Server Components, it's important to understand that cookies are fundamentally a client-side storage mechanism: 78 79 - **Reading cookies** works in Server Components because you're accessing the cookie data that the client's browser sends to the server in the HTTP request headers. 80 - **Setting cookies** is not supported during Server Component rendering. To modify cookies, invoke a Server Function from the client or use a Route Handler. 81 82 The server can only send instructions (via `Set-Cookie` headers) to tell the browser to store cookies - the actual storage happens on the client side. This is why cookie operations that modify state (`.set`, `.delete`) must be performed in a Server Function or Route Handler where the response headers can be properly set. 83 84 ## Understanding Cookie Behavior in Server Functions 85 86 After you set or delete a cookie in a Server Function, Next.js can return both the updated UI and new data in a single server roundtrip when the function is used as a [Server Action](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data#what-are-server-functions) (e.g., passed to a form's `action` prop). See [Caching and Revalidating](/docs/app/getting-started/caching). 87 88 The UI is not unmounted, but effects that depend on data coming from the server will re-run. 89 90 To refresh cached data too, call [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) or [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) inside the function. 91 92 ## Examples 93 94 ### Getting a cookie 95 96 You can use the `(await cookies()).get('name')` method to get a single cookie: 97 98 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 99 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 100 101 export default async function Page() { 102 const cookieStore = await cookies() 103 const theme = cookieStore.get('theme') 104 return '...' 105 } 106 ``` 107 108 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 109 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 110 111 export default async function Page() { 112 const cookieStore = await cookies() 113 const theme = cookieStore.get('theme') 114 return '...' 115 } 116 ``` 117 118 ### Getting all cookies 119 120 You can use the `(await cookies()).getAll()` method to get all cookies with a matching name. If `name` is unspecified, it returns all the available cookies. 121 122 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 123 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 124 125 export default async function Page() { 126 const cookieStore = await cookies() 127 return cookieStore.getAll().map((cookie) => ( 128
129

131
132 )) 133 } 134 ``` 135 136 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 137 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 138 139 export default async function Page() { 140 const cookieStore = await cookies() 141 return cookieStore.getAll().map((cookie) => ( 142
143

146 )) 147 } 148 ``` 149 150 ### Setting a cookie 151 152 You can use the `(await cookies()).set(name, value, options)` method in a [Server Function](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) to set a cookie. The [`options` object](#options) is optional. 153 154 ```tsx filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 155 'use server' 156 157 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 158 159 export async function create(data) { 160 const cookieStore = await cookies() 161 162 cookieStore.set('name', 'lee') 163 // or 164 cookieStore.set('name', 'lee', { secure: true }) 165 // or 166 cookieStore.set({ 167 name: 'name', 168 value: 'lee', 169 httpOnly: true, 170 path: '/', 171 }) 172 } 173 ``` 174 175 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 176 'use server' 177 178 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 179 cookieStore.set({ 188 name: 'name', 189 value: 'lee', 190 httpOnly: true, 191 path: '/', 192 }) 193 } 194 ``` 195 196 ### Checking if a cookie exists 197 198 You can use the `(await cookies()).has(name)` method to check if a cookie exists: 199 200 ```tsx filename="app/page.ts" switcher 201 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 202 203 export default async function Page() { 204 const cookieStore = await cookies() 205 const hasCookie = cookieStore.has('theme') 206 return '...' 207 } 208 ``` 209 210 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 211 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 212 213 export default async function Page() { 214 const cookieStore = await cookies() 215 const hasCookie = cookieStore.has('theme') 216 return '...' 217 } 218 ``` 219 220 ### Deleting cookies 221 222 There are three ways you can delete a cookie. 223 224 Using the `delete()` method: 225 226 ```tsx filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 227 'use server' 228 229 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 230 231 export async function deleteCookie(data) { 232 const cookieStore = await cookies() 233 cookieStore.delete('name') 234 } 235 ``` 236 237 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 238 'use server' 239 240 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 241 242 export async function deleteCookie(data) { 243 const cookieStore = await cookies() 244 cookieStore.delete('name') 245 } 246 ``` 247 248 Setting a new cookie with the same name and an empty value: 249 250 ```tsx filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 251 'use server' 252 253 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 254 255 export async function deleteCookie(data) { 256 const cookieStore = await cookies() 257 cookieStore.set('name', '') 258 } 259 ``` 260 261 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 262 'use server' 263 264 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 265 266 export async function deleteCookie(data) { 267 const cookieStore = await cookies() 268 cookieStore.set('name', '') 269 } 270 ``` 271 272 Setting the `maxAge` to 0 will immediately expire a cookie. `maxAge` accepts a value in seconds. 273 274 ```tsx filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 275 'use server' 276 277 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 278 279 export async function deleteCookie(data) { 280 const cookieStore = await cookies() 281 cookieStore.set('name', 'value', { maxAge: 0 }) 282 } 283 ``` 284 285 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 286 'use server' 287 288 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 289 290 export async function deleteCookie(data) { 291 const cookieStore = await cookies() 292 cookieStore.set('name', 'value', { maxAge: 0 }) 293 } 294 ``` 295 296 ## Version History 297 298 | Version | Changes | 299 | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | 300 | `v15.0.0-RC` | `cookies` is now an async function. A [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#150) is available. | 301 | `v13.0.0` | `cookies` introduced. | 302

1 --- 2 title: headers 3 description: API reference for the headers function. 4 --- 5 6 `headers` is an **async** function that allows you to **read** the HTTP incoming request headers from a [Server Component](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components). 7 8 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 9 import { headers } from 'next/headers' 10 11 export default async function Page() { 12 const headersList = await headers() 13 const userAgent = headersList.get('user-agent') 14 } 15 ``` 16 17 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 18 import { headers } from 'next/headers' 19 20 export default async function Page() { 21 const headersList = await headers() 22 const userAgent = headersList.get('user-agent') 23 } 24 ``` 25 26 ## Reference 27 28 ### Parameters 29 30 `headers` does not take any parameters. 31 32 ### Returns 33 34 `headers` returns a **read-only** [Web Headers](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers) object. 35 36 - [`Headers.entries()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/entries): Returns an [`iterator`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Iteration_protocols) allowing to go through all key/value pairs contained in this object. 37 - [`Headers.forEach()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/forEach): Executes a provided function once for each key/value pair in this `Headers` object. 38 - [`Headers.get()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/get): Returns a [`String`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/String) sequence of all the values of a header within a `Headers` object with a given name. 39 - [`Headers.has()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/has): Returns a boolean stating whether a `Headers` object contains a certain header. 40 - [`Headers.keys()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/keys): Returns an [`iterator`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Iteration_protocols) allowing you to go through all keys of the key/value pairs contained in this object. 41 - [`Headers.values()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/values): Returns an [`iterator`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Iteration_protocols) allowing you to go through all values of the key/value pairs contained in this object. 42 43 ## Good to know 44 45 - `headers` is an **asynchronous** function that returns a promise. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function. 46 - In version 14 and earlier, `headers` was a synchronous function. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future. 47 - Since `headers` is read-only, you cannot `set` or `delete` the outgoing request headers. 48 - `headers` is a [Request-time API](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) whose returned values cannot be known ahead of time. Using it in will opt a route into **[dynamic rendering](/docs/app/glossary#dynamic-rendering)**. 49 50 ## Examples 51 52 ### Using the Authorization header 53 54 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" 55 import { headers } from 'next/headers' 56 57 export default async function Page() { 58 const authorization = (await headers()).get('authorization') 59 const res = await fetch('...', { 60 headers: { authorization }, // Forward the authorization header 61 }) 62 const user = await res.json() 63 64 return

{user.name}

65 } 66 ``` 67 68 ## Version History 69 70 | Version | Changes | 71 | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | 72 | `v15.0.0-RC` | `headers` is now an async function. --- title: headers description: API reference for the headers function. --- `headers` is an **async** function that allows you to **read** the HTTP incoming request headers from a [Server Component](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components). ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher import { headers } from 'next/headers' export default async function Page() { const headersList = await headers() const userAgent = headersList.get('user-agent') } ``` ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher import { headers } from 'next/headers' export default async function Page() { const headersList = await headers() const userAgent = headersList.get('user-agent') } ``` ## Reference ### Parameters `headers` does not take any parameters. ### Returns `headers` returns a **read-only** [Web Headers](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers) object. - [`Headers.entries()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/entries): Returns an [`iterator`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Iteration_protocols) allowing to go through all key/value pairs contained in this object. - [`Headers.forEach()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/forEach): Executes a provided function once for each key/value pair in this `Headers` object. - [`Headers.get()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/get): Returns a [`String`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/String) sequence of all the values of a header within a `Headers` object with a given name. - [`Headers.has()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/has): Returns a boolean stating whether a `Headers` object contains a certain header. - [`Headers.keys()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/keys): Returns an [`iterator`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Iteration_protocols) allowing you to go through all keys of the key/value pairs contained in this object. - [`Headers.values()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/values): Returns an [`iterator`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Iteration_protocols) allowing you to go through all values of the key/value pairs contained in this object. ## Good to know - `headers` is an **asynchronous** function that returns a promise. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function. - In version 14 and earlier, `headers` was a synchronous function. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future. - Since `headers` is read-only, you cannot `set` or `delete` the outgoing request headers. - `headers` is a [Request-time API](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) whose returned values cannot be known ahead of time. Using it in will opt a route into **[dynamic rendering](/docs/app/glossary#dynamic-rendering)**. ## Examples ### Using the Authorization header ```jsx filename="app/page.js" import { headers } from 'next/headers' export default async function Page() { const authorization = (await headers()).get('authorization') const res = await fetch('...', { headers: { authorization }, // Forward the authorization header }) const user = await res.json() return

{user.name}

} ``` ## Version History | Version | Changes | | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `v15.0.0-RC` | `headers` is now an async function. A [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#150) is available. | | `v13.0.0` | `headers` introduced. |

**Key detail for this Next.js version (16 canary):** I checked `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` first as `AGENTS.md` requires. Using these request-time APIs also opts the route into dynamic rendering, which is correct here since the output depends on the incoming request.

- Parses the `Accept-Language` header, taking the highest-priority tag (e.g. `en-US` from `en-US,en;q=0.9`), falling back to `"unknown"` if the header is missing.
